tasks.title: Install Required Packages: @tanstack/react-query, @tanstack/react-query-devtools, and react-hot-toast
tasks.description: Install and configure the required npm packages (@tanstack/react-query, @tanstack/react-query-devtools, and react-hot-toast) as specified in section 2.2.1 of the PRD.
tasks.details:
1. Use npm or yarn to install the following packages:
   - @tanstack/react-query: For efficient data fetching, caching, and state management
   - @tanstack/react-query-devtools: For debugging and monitoring React Query operations
   - react-hot-toast: For displaying toast notifications in the application

2. After installation, set up the React Query provider in the application's main component:
   - Import QueryClient and QueryClientProvider from @tanstack/react-query
   - Create a new QueryClient instance
   - Wrap the application with QueryClientProvider

3. Configure the React Query DevTools:
   - Import ReactQueryDevtools from @tanstack/react-query-devtools
   - Add the DevTools component inside the QueryClientProvider (only in development environment)

4. Set up the Toaster component from react-hot-toast:
   - Import Toaster from react-hot-toast
   - Add the Toaster component to the application's main component

5. Document any specific configuration requirements mentioned in section 2.2.1 of the PRD.

6. Update the project's package.json and ensure the dependencies are properly listed.

1. Verify package installation:
   - Check package.json to confirm the packages are listed with correct versions
   - Ensure node_modules contains the installed packages

2. Verify React Query setup:

   - Check that a QueryClient instance is created correctly

3. Verify React Query DevTools:

tasks.details:

For Admin Components:
1. Update `src/client/components/admin/students/StudentList.tsx`, `src/client/components/admin/students/StudentForm.tsx`, and `src/client/components/admin/students/StudentDetail.tsx` to use the `useStudentsQuery` hook for fetching and manipulating student data.
2. Update `src/client/components/admin/topics/TopicList.tsx` and `src/client/components/admin/topics/TopicForm.tsx` to use the `useTopicsQuery` hook for topic-related operations.
3. Update `src/client/components/admin/lessons/LessonList.tsx` and `src/client/components/admin/lessons/LessonForm.tsx` to use the `useLessonsQuery` hook for lesson data management.
4. Update `src/client/components/admin/CourseManager.tsx` to use the `useCoursesQuery` hook for course management operations.

tasks.title: Implement React Query DevTools for Development Environment
tasks.description: Install and configure React Query DevTools in the development environment to support debugging and optimization of queries as specified in PRD section 5.3.
tasks.details:
This task involves implementing React Query DevTools to enhance the development experience by providing visual tools for query debugging and optimization.

Steps to complete:
1. Install the required package: `@tanstack/react-query-devtools`
2. Modify the existing ReactQueryProvider component (created in Task #4) to conditionally include the DevTools component in development mode only
3. Configure the DevTools with appropriate settings as specified in PRD section 5.3
4. Ensure the DevTools panel is accessible in the UI during development
5. Implement proper environment detection to prevent DevTools from being included in production builds
6. Add documentation in the codebase explaining how to use the DevTools for debugging queries
7. Update the ReactQueryProvider component to expose any necessary configuration options for the DevTools

The implementation should follow best practices for React Query DevTools integration, ensuring it doesn't affect production performance while providing comprehensive debugging capabilities during development.
tasks.testStrategy:
Testing strategy for this task:

1. Manual verification:
   - Run the application in development mode and confirm the React Query DevTools panel appears in the UI
   - Verify that all query states, cache information, and debugging tools are properly displayed
   - Test the DevTools functionality by interacting with various queries in the application
   - Confirm that the DevTools UI matches the specifications in PRD section 5.3

2. Automated testing:
   - Write unit tests for the ReactQueryProvider component to verify it correctly includes DevTools in development mode
   - Create tests that verify DevTools are not included in production builds
   - Test that the DevTools configuration matches the requirements

3. Integration testing:
   - Verify that the DevTools integration doesn't interfere with normal application functionality
   - Test that query debugging information is accurately displayed for various query states (loading, error, success)

4. Code review checklist:
   - Confirm proper conditional rendering based on environment
   - Verify that DevTools are not included in production bundles
   - Check that the implementation follows the React Query documentation guidelines
   - Ensure the code is optimized to minimize impact on development performance

tasks.title: Task #25: Optimize React Query Configuration and Data Fetching Strategies
tasks.description: Optimize React Query configuration and data fetching strategies to minimize unnecessary re-renders and improve application performance according to PRD section 5.5.
tasks.details:
This task involves a comprehensive review and optimization of the React Query implementation across the application:

1. Review current React Query configuration:
   - Analyze the existing queryClient configuration
   - Identify default settings that can be optimized (staleTime, cacheTime, refetchOnWindowFocus, etc.)
   - Review query key structure for proper cache management

2. Implement performance optimizations:
   - Configure optimal staleTime and cacheTime values based on data volatility
   - Implement selective query invalidation strategies to prevent cascade re-fetching
   - Use query deduplication for identical requests
   - Implement proper error boundaries and retry logic
   - Optimize dependent queries with enabled option

3. Reduce unnecessary re-renders:
   - Implement data transformation in select functions to prevent re-renders from unrelated data changes
   - Use structural sharing options to minimize new object creation
   - Apply React.memo and useMemo where appropriate with React Query results
   - Implement pagination and infinite queries for large data sets

4. Implement advanced caching strategies:
   - Configure prefetching for anticipated user actions
   - Implement optimistic updates for better UX during mutations
   - Use placeholderData or initialData where appropriate
   - Configure proper query key factories for consistent cache management

5. Documentation and knowledge sharing:
   - Document all optimization strategies implemented
   - Create performance benchmarks before and after optimizations
   - Update team guidelines for React Query usage

This task builds upon the React Query hooks implementation from Tasks #21 and #22, focusing specifically on performance optimization rather than basic implementation.
tasks.testStrategy:
The optimization efforts should be verified through a multi-faceted testing approach:

1. Performance metrics measurement:
   - Use React DevTools Profiler to measure and compare render counts before and after optimizations
   - Implement and run Lighthouse performance tests in CI pipeline
   - Use React Query DevTools to verify proper caching behavior and identify unnecessary refetches
   - Measure and document Time to Interactive (TTI) improvements

2. Automated testing:
   - Create unit tests for optimized query hooks to verify caching behavior
   - Implement integration tests that verify data consistency with optimized fetching
   - Create performance regression tests to prevent future performance degradation

3. Load testing:
   - Simulate high-load scenarios to verify application stability under stress
   - Test with throttled network conditions to verify optimized loading states
   - Measure memory usage patterns before and after optimizations

4. User experience validation:
   - Conduct A/B testing with optimized vs. non-optimized versions
   - Measure and compare key UX metrics (page load time, time to first meaningful paint)
   - Document perceived performance improvements

5. Code review:
   - Conduct thorough code reviews focusing on React Query best practices
   - Verify proper implementation of memoization techniques
   - Ensure consistent query key strategies across the application

All test results should be documented with before/after comparisons to quantify the performance improvements achieved.
